final_message:
I've written the Bluebird Bakery draft for September 2026 and saved both files to `evals/runs/clean-run-20261012/c_bb_subtotal_mismatch/skill_output/`:
- `bluebird-bakery-co-2026-09-trends.md` is the report, marked DRAFT, with my commentary in section 1.
- `bluebird-bakery-co-2026-09-trends.json` holds every figure the report uses.

**Data quality: one subtotal doesn't match.** In March 2026, "Total for Professional Services" states 2,225, but the lines under it add up to 2,200 (a 25 difference). The analysis uses 2,200; the reviewer needs to decide which is right. Gross profit and net income match the workbook's own totals in every month, and the balance sheet balances. Part of the structure was rebuilt by the script, and the commentary asks the reviewer to confirm both:
- "Total Delivery" had no heading row, so its group was rebuilt from the two lines above it.
- "Charitable Donations" had no total row, so it was treated as a blank account.

**Main points:**
- **Revenue was 81,300**, up 17.7% on August and 17.3% above the previous six-month average. Most of the jump is a new stream, Wholesale Accounts, at 12,000. There's no same-month-last-year comparison because the export only covers nine months.
- **Gross margin was 65.3%**, up 5.7 points on August and the highest of the period.
- **Payroll rose to 22,600**, up 28.4% (+5,000), after five flat months. All of it is in Wages & Salaries. The reviewer should confirm whether this is the new normal or a one-month item.
- **Cash in the bank fell to 37,600**: down 1,800 on August and 10,800 on six months ago, even though the business made a profit every month. Equity also went down. I've left the gap between profit and cash as a question for the reviewer, since the export doesn't show the cause.

**"Other" category:** three expense accounts didn't match any category rule: Instagram Ads, Mystery Shopper Program and Supplier Rebates. Mystery Shopper Program looks like a new cost in the tables, but it also appears in March and June, so I described it as quarterly rather than new.
